To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the accuracy of binary networks can be significantly improved by using a strong baseline, (2) by matching the output of the real and binary convolutions, and, (3) by using the real activations during inference to re-scale the binary activations.

(i) the discrepancy between the binary and real convolutional layers, which is usually discarded in the binarization literature, is a source of significant accuracy gains; (ii) this discrepancy can be exploited during training with a novel loss function, and during inference by using the real activations prior to the binaring process.

(1) the discrepancy between the activations of a binary and a real-valued convolution is a useful signal to minimize during training, and (2), by doing so, it is possible to train a binary network to within a few percentage points of the real-valued counterpart.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1. Can binary neural networks achieve state-of-the-art results?
the design of binary neural networks that can be trained to within a few percentage points of their real-valued counterpart.
the problem of training a deep neural network to perform a binary operation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown how to train binary neural networks to within a small margin of their full precision counterparts.
we show how to train binary neural networks to within a 3-5% top- 1 accuracy gap of their real-valued counterpart, which we believe is the most important result of our work.
the authors have developed a novel method that improves the accuracy of binary neural networks by a large margin, making them more competitive and practical for real-world applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel training strategy to train binary neural networks that outperforms the current state of art by 3-5%, and we show how to use this strategy to train binary networks with real-to- binary convolutions.

we show that the gap between real-valued and binary networks can be reduced from 10% to 3% by carefully combining recent advances and by introducing two novel techniques: a loss function to match the spatial attention maps and a data-driven re-scaling technique.
we show how to train binary neural networks to within a 3% top-1 error on CIFAR-10, a 5% top 1 error on CIFER-100 and a 5% error on ImageNet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy gap to full precision models can be reduced to a few percent points, which opens the door to the use of binary models in real-world applications.
, when using the right loss functions and optimization procedures, binary networks can achieve state-of-the-art performance.

, with a careful optimization procedure and a good initialization, binary networks can be trained to a very high level of accuracy, and that this accuracy can be further improved by minimizing the discrepancy between the real and binary convolutional layers.
